question: Life expectancy rose worldwide between the 1930s and the 1960s. How much did Samuel Preston credit to higher incomes?
options: About a tenth to a quarter
answer: About a tenth to a quarter. At the same income, countries in the 1960s lived far longer than countries had in the 1930s. The rest came from things money alone did not buy: vaccines, antibiotics, clean water and knowing how disease spreads. Rich countries live longer, but wealth is not the whole recipe.
move: Two things rising together can both be riding a third.
ask: Which good thing in my life do I credit to money, when something cheaper may be doing the work?
trap: Most of it, since richer countries clearly live longer.
reference: Preston, The changing relation between mortality and level of economic development, Population Studies, 1975
